ar_SA: Modern Standard Arabic. Clear desktop terminology, concise labels, natural RTL punctuation. Preserve product names and commands.
de_DE: Natural informal German. Use du consistently. Prefer established Linux and desktop terms. Preserve product names such as Waffle and Material ii.
es_AR: Natural Argentine Spanish with consistent voseo. Avoid slang and exaggerated regionalisms. Use established Linux terminology. Keep shell when it names the technical desktop-shell layer, and preserve product terms such as Pill, Waffle and Cookie.
fr_FR: Natural concise French. Use vous consistently in instructions. Prefer established desktop terminology and avoid English syntax calques.
he_HE: Natural modern Hebrew. Concise RTL UI language. Preserve product names, commands and technical acronyms.
hi_IN: Natural standard Hindi suitable for a Linux desktop. Keep common technical product names and commands in Latin script when that is clearer.
it_IT: Natural informal Italian. Use tu consistently. Prefer established Linux and desktop terms and concise settings descriptions.
ja_JP: Natural compact Japanese UI language. Avoid unnecessary pronouns and literal English word order. Preserve product names and commands in Latin script.
ko_KR: Natural concise Korean UI language with consistent polite explanatory style. Preserve product names, commands and technical acronyms.
pt_BR: Natural Brazilian Portuguese with consistent você. Prefer established Linux and desktop terms and concise labels.
ru_RU: Natural concise Russian UI language. Use established Linux terminology and consistent neutral instructions. Preserve product names and commands.
uk_UA: Natural concise Ukrainian UI language. Use established Linux terminology and avoid Russian calques. Preserve product names and commands.
vi_VN: Natural concise Vietnamese UI language. Prefer established desktop terminology and preserve product names, commands and technical acronyms.
zh_CN: Natural concise Simplified Chinese UI language. Avoid literal English syntax. Preserve product names, commands and technical acronyms when customary.
